Thanks again for the call this morning — helpful intro. A few items we wanted to capture so we can align with our eng team: 

1) Auth & SDK setup
- Are there recommended patterns for short-lived credentials vs long-lived API keys for our server-side calls? We need to support both CI services and an internal service mesh.

2) Routing & model variants
- We liked the idea of smart routing (latency/cost tiers). How do you recommend we configure the client to prefer lower-cost variants but fail over to higher-quality models on error?

3) Structured output / tool calling
- We'll need structured json outputs (for downstream parsers) and some tool-calling hooks so the model can call our internal lookup service. Any SDK guidance on deterministic tool results?

4) Embeddings + reranker
- We're planning to embed FT documents at index-time and do a rerank step. Do you have recommended embedding dimensionality and latency-cost tradeoffs?

5) Observability hooks
- Most important: trace correlation. Can you provide the header names and recommended fields to log (trace id, token-level latency, KV cache hits, routing decision)? Example headers we'd like to see in responses and logs.

Attached: rough architecture sketch we drew during the call (redwood_arch_sketch.png).

Next steps for us: share this with our platform team and ask for a short SE session on SDK auth and sample telemetry output. Can you also share any sample dashboards for per-route latency and per-model token breakdowns?

Amit — great to meet you earlier. High-level answers and proposed next steps below. I'll book a short SE session with Dev for next week (30-45m) to walk through SDK auth and telemetry examples.

Quick answers:
- Auth: we support API keys, short-lived tokens (STS), and mTLS for Private deployments. For CI/service mesh we typically recommend short-lived tokens rotated by your identity provider; long-lived keys only for isolated service accounts with strict ACLs.

- Routing: our client SDK accepts a routing policy object (priority list + fallback rules). Example policy: prefer "redwood-small" for cost, fallback to "redwood-medium" on expected latency > 250ms or error. We can share a sample policy.

- Structured outputs/tool calling: we support function/tool-calling schema in the response envelope. Client-side validation helpers exist to assert deterministic tool outputs (e.g., required fields + types).

- Embeddings/reranker: typical guidance — 768/1024 dims for semantic search with small-medium corpora; 1536+ for high-signal reranks where nuance matters. We recommend an initial A/B on dimension and quantization settings to measure latency vs recall.

- Observability headers: we recommend sending a request header X-Redwood-Client-TraceId (UUID) and X-Request-Source (service-name). On responses we return X-Redwood-TraceId, X-Redwood-Latency-Breakdown (comma-separated tokens:queue_ms,decode_ms,kv_cache_ms,network_ms), and X-Redwood-Model-Variant. Logs include token-count, rerank-latency_ms, and cache_hit=true/false.

Attachments/links I'll share before the SE session:
- SDK quickstart snippet (node/python)
- Sample routing policy JSON
- Dashboard screenshots (per-route latency + token breakdown)

Proposed next steps:
1) SE session w/ Dev & FinTechCo platform (30-45m) — I'll propose times for Tues/Wed next week.
2) Share MAP (mutual action plan) and a short integration checklist for your platform team.
3) If useful, we can prepare a small PoC with a short-lived token example and a dashboard with example traces.

I'll attach the MAP and a sample dashboard link in the follow-up. Does Tuesday 2026-06-30 10:00 PT work for you?

Amit — quick technical notes ahead of the SE call. I'll walk through these live but wanted to put some implementable details here so your engs can review.

1) Trace correlation
- Client should generate X-Redwood-Client-TraceId (UUID v4). If you already propagate X-Request-ID in your mesh, map that -> X-Redwood-Client-TraceId.
- Response headers we set: X-Redwood-TraceId (matches client id or a server side uuid if not provided), X-Redwood-Latency-Breakdown: "queue_ms=12,kv_cache_ms=5,compile_ms=0,decode_ms=48,network_ms=7". Use these fields to populate your dashboard.

2) Logging fields we recommend capturing per request
- trace_id, request_id, model_variant, tokens_in, tokens_out, kv_cache_hit (true/false), routing_decision (policy name), latency_ms_total, latency_breakdown (as above).

3) Embeddings + rerank flow suggestion
- Index time: compute embeddings (dim 1024), store vector + doc_id.
- Query time: compute query embedding, NN search top-100, then rerank top-10 with a cross-encoder on full context (or use our reranker endpoint). Measure rerank latency; if > 120ms consider reducing candidate set.

4) Structured outputs / tool calling
- Use response field "tools" (JSON array) and include a deterministic schema for each tool. If the model uses a tool, it will emit a tool_call with name and args; the SDK provides a verifier to assert required keys.

5) SDK snippets
- Node example header insertion:
  const traceId = uuidv4();
  fetch(url, { headers: { 'Authorization': `Bearer ${API_KEY}`, 'X-Redwood-Client-TraceId': traceId } });

I'll bring a sample dashboard link and a minimal PoC repo to the call. If you want the PoC before the call, say the word and I can push a branch.

—Dev
